findings.message: India 256GB price (₹38,999) misattributed to Beebom; only TechCabal's snapshot states it
findings.details: Body text ("What We Know" section) reads: 'priced at ₹34,999 for the 8GB/128GB model and ₹38,999 for the 8GB/256GB model, [according to Beebom]'. Beebom's snapshot (source-4.html.gz) confirms ₹34,999/8GB-128GB but never mentions ₹38,999 or a 256GB storage option — Beebom's India product page only lists a single 8GB/128GB SKU. The ₹38,999/256GB figure is stated verbatim in TechCabal's snapshot (source-1.html.gz): 'India: ₹34,999 for the 8GB RAM and 128GB storage model, and ₹38,999 for the 8GB RAM and 256GB model.' The fact is true and verifiable, but cited to the wrong outlet. Not in the headline, summary, or lead — a subordinate detail in the body. Filed as a corrections record rather than blocking publication.

content_preview.summary: Nothing's Phone (4b) went on sale at its London store on July 11 at £299/€329, pairing a 5,200mAh battery (6,000mAh in India) with a 45-LED Glyph Bar; the company has not confirmed a US launch.

The London-based consumer electronics company unveiled the phone globally on July 7 through a livestream event, [according to TechCabal](https://techcabal.com/2026/07/07/nothing-phone-4b-price-release-date-specs/). editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News-category piece using the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure. 624 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Prose is clear, specifics are dense but readable, and the Analysis section fairly represents two contrasting outside assessments (9to5Google's harsh take vs. Gizmochina's more charitable framing) rather than injecting the bot's own opinion.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 8 cited sources were fetched successfully (HTTP 200, no archive fallbacks) and every gzip snapshot's sha256 matched the manifest. I decompressed and read all 8 snapshots in full (source-0.html.gz through source-7.html.gz) rather than re-fetching live URLs. Verified claim-by-claim against snapshot text: (1) Tech Advisor (source-0) confirms the July 11 London-store launch ahead of the July 17 wider rollout, £299/€329 pricing, 45 mini-LEDs across four Glyph Bar zones, and the 'not going to be available in the US' framing. (2) TechCabal (source-1) confirms the July 7 livestream unveil, 6.77-inch 120Hz/2000-nit AMOLED display, Nothing OS 4.1 on Android 16 with 3yr/6yr update commitment, 5,200mAh global vs 6,000mAh India battery split, and Germany/Austria €329 vs Switzerland CHF 299 pricing — and additionally contains the ₹38,999/256GB India price (see Attribution finding below). (3) Telecompaper (source-2, paywalled preview) confirms GBP 299/EUR 329/INR 29,999 pricing, 8GB+128GB base configuration, and black/white/blue color options. (4) Android Police (source-3) confirms the £299 UK price, the verbatim quote 'It has not been announced for release in the US,' the Phone (4a)'s £349 launch price, and the 8.6mm/210g dimensions. (5) Beebom (source-4) confirms the Snapdragon 6 Gen 4 chipset, 8GB RAM, 50MP OIS main + 8MP ultrawide + 16MP front camera specs, 33W wired/7.5W reverse-wired charging, and the ₹34,999 India price/July 14 Flipkart availability — but does NOT contain the ₹38,999/256GB figure attributed to it (flagged as a misattribution finding). (6) Nothing's own product page (source-5) confirms both verbatim quotes used in the article: 'Our longest-lasting battery' and 'the focus-saving Glyph Bar.' (7) 9to5Google (source-6) confirms the 128GB/256GB UFS 2.2 storage option and both verbatim review quotes: 'a pretty simple step down from Phone (4a)' and 'impossible to recommend buying Phone (4b) when Phone (4a) is better for basically the same price.' (8) Gizmochina (source-7) confirms both verbatim quotes: 'a slightly different Glyph Bar layout' and 'the more premium mid-ranger, while the 4b focuses on value with a bigger battery.' No snapshot fetch failures occurred, so no live-URL fallback was needed. I also confirmed the internal link to the April 3, 2026 Nothing smart-glasses article resolves to a real, on-topic prior article in the archive.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: One specific was misattributed: the ₹38,999 8GB/256GB India price is cited to Beebom but only appears in TechCabal's snapshot; Beebom's own India product page lists just a single 8GB/128GB SKU at ₹34,999. The fact itself is true and independently verifiable (it is stated plainly in the TechCabal snapshot already cited elsewhere in the same paragraph's neighboring sentences), so this is a citation error rather than a fabrication. It sits in the body ('What We Know' section), not the headline, summary, or Overview lead. Every other specific, number, and direct quote I checked (headline £299/5,200mAh/45-LED claims, London July 11 date, July 17 rollout, US non-availability, Phone (4a) £349 comparison, both Nothing.tech quotes, both 9to5Google review quotes, both Gizmochina quotes) traced cleanly to its cited source. No hallucinated quotes found. Note: TechCabal's own article separately states UK/US pricing was 'not confirmed' as of its July 7 writing, which superficially conflicts with Tech Advisor's and Android Police's same-week reporting of a firm £299 UK price — but the submission never cites TechCabal for the UK price (it cites Telecompaper and is independently corroborated by Tech Advisor and Android Police), so this is a cross-outlet reporting discrepancy rather than a sourcing error in the submission.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing beyond attributed critical/positive framing from named outlets, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for prior Phone (4b) or 'Phone 4b' coverage; none found. This is the first Machine Herald article on this launch. The Analysis section correctly links to a genuinely related April 3, 2026 article on Nothing's smart-glasses/earbuds strategy rather than re-covering it.
concerns: The ₹38,999/8GB-256GB India price is attributed to Beebom in the body but only appears in TechCabal's source snapshot; Beebom's snapshot only supports the ₹34,999/8GB-128GB figure. Filing a corrections record to fix the attribution.
recommendations: Consider adding techadvisor.com, techcabal.com, telecompaper.com, androidpolice.com, gadgets.beebom.com, gizmochina.com, and nothing.tech to config/source_allowlist.txt — all seven are legitimate, verifiable tech-journalism or manufacturer sources that were fully verified in this review; the allowlist warning is a coverage gap, not a credibility issue.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate, well-sourced, neutral News piece with one recoverable citation error (a real India price figure attributed to the wrong of two adjacent outlets). Approving with a corrections record filed for the misattributed ₹38,999/256GB price.
